summary: A survey and tutorial on connectionless data transmission, where each message is sent on its own without first setting up a connection. It was circulated for review ahead of a proposed US position urging that the OSI model include this style of communication.

eli5.summary: Some networks work like a phone call and some like postcards. This paper explains the postcard style and argues it deserves a place in the standard.

questions: where do connectionless services appear in osi
subtitle: Why the OSI model should embrace message-at-a-time communication.

tldr.problem: The OSI Reference Model assumed all communication requires setting up connections first, but many important applications work better by sending individual messages without negotiation.
tldr.mechanism: Connectionless data transmission sends self-contained messages directly without three-way agreements, prior negotiation, or delivery guarantees. The RFC surveys applications like sensor monitoring, request-response systems, and local area networks where this model excels.
tldr.outcome: The RFC advocates that connectionless services should be incorporated at multiple layers of the OSI stack as a complementary concept alongside connection-oriented services, enabling a broader range of application designs.

today: RFC 787 was circulated for review ahead of standards work on the OSI model. Connectionless services were subsequently incorporated into OSI standards and became foundational to modern network design, especially in Internet protocols and local area networks.

sections.title: The OSI Reference Model and Connection Orientation
sections.content: The OSI (Open Systems Interconnection) Reference Model, under development by ISO and other standards bodies, organizes communication into seven layers, each providing services to the layer above it. Connections—associations established between two or more entities that support data transfer over a period of time—have been fundamental to the model's architecture. However, RFC 787 argues that connections are not universally necessary and that the model should embrace connectionless data transmission as a complementary paradigm.
sections.eli5: The OSI model is like a library with seven shelves of rules. Each shelf gives services to the shelf above it. The model was built assuming you need to set up a connection first, like dialing a phone. This paper argues that's not always necessary.

sections.title: Connection-Oriented vs. Connectionless Communication
sections.content: Connection-oriented interactions proceed through three distinct phases: connection establishment (negotiation of parameters), data transfer, and release. They maintain a relationship between data units: each message is tied to a specific connection, and messages can be ordered and related to each other. Connectionless data transmission, by contrast, is a single operation requiring no prior negotiation. Each message is self-contained—it carries all routing and addressing information within itself—and bears no logical relationship to other messages. The service provider makes no attempt to guarantee delivery, maintain order, or prevent duplicates. Applications provide their own recovery mechanisms if needed.
sections.eli5: Connections are like a conversation: you introduce yourselves, agree on what you'll talk about, have a discussion, and say goodbye. Connectionless is like shouting a message into a room: anyone listening hears it, but you don't know who or whether they understood.

sections.title: Applications That Demand Connectionless Service
sections.content: The RFC identifies seven categories of applications suited to connectionless transmission. Inward data collection involves many sensors or monitors reporting to a central point; occasional lost readings are acceptable because the next one arrives soon. Outward data dissemination broadcasts a single message to many destinations at low cost. Request-response systems (point-of-sale terminals, credit checking, reservation systems) typically involve a single query and response without unnecessary protocol overhead. Broadcast and multicast communication—where group addressing is essential—is awkward with connection-oriented models. Applications with inherent redundancy, such as digitized voice or telemetry, can tolerate occasional lost data. Local area networks benefit from connectionless services because their reliable, short-range media make the model simpler and cheaper to implement. Finally, network interconnection (internetworking) is simplified when gateways treat each packet independently without maintaining connection state.
sections.eli5: Connectionless works great for things like taking temperature readings every few seconds, broadcasting alerts to many computers, answering customer questions one at a time, or talking on a reliable local network where messages almost never get lost.

sections.title: Connectionless Services in the OSI Layers
sections.content: The RFC examines where connectionless services should appear in the OSI stack. At the data link layer, connectionless service suits local area networks with their intrinsically reliable media and broadcast nature; the IEEE 802 LAN standard proposes both connection-oriented and connectionless procedures. At the network layer, connectionless service simplifies design by making few assumptions about underlying services, facilitating dynamic routing, and enabling the local-net-independence principle. At higher layers (session and presentation), connectionless service is primarily valuable to pass a connectionless flow through to applications that need it. At the application layer, connectionless services enable direct request-response interactions and support system management tasks. The RFC proposes that conversion between connection-oriented and connectionless modes be permitted at the network, transport, and application layers, while other layers employ the same service type they receive from below.
sections.eli5: Local networks, the internet layer, and applications all benefit most. Other layers just need to pass the service through without changing it.
